f54ec608d64c.title: FHIR content
f54ec608d64c.content: TR… . On this page . | Representations, and why only one is taken | The artefact index is reconstructed | Where the rules live | . This page is generated from docs/source/fhir-fhir-content/ — each section below links to its own source. ✎ Edit QA… TR… . A FHIR Implementation Guide is a published, versioned package of profiles, terminology, examples and prose that says how FHIR is to be used for one purpose. This page describes how IG content is shaped in the graph. Two things distinguish it from the other content kinds here. It is compiled — an author writes FHIR Shorthand and a tool produces the resources, so the thing an author edits and the thing a reader fetches are different artefacts. And it is published at canonical URLs that other IGs resolve against, so its identity is a URL and a version rather than a path in a repository.

72102ff376f3.title: Representations, and why only one is taken
72102ff376f3.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The IG Publisher emits three serialisations of every resource — JSON, XML and Turtle — plus HTML per resource page. Only the JSON is taken, wrapped in JSON-LD and JSON Schema; RDF, where needed, is projected from the JSON-LD. The site neither renders nor links a resource’s XML or Turtle copy. A representation that arrives and is not taken is recorded as a refusal. The Publisher’s per-page HTML is a rendering, not a serialisation, and is not used: it has no front matter, so the navbar, language bar, QA badges and translation surface cannot reach it. IG pages are rendered as folio pages instead (see ig-render-jekyll).

3744f26cc500.title: The artefact index is reconstructed
3744f26cc500.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . No FHIR IG publishes an index of its own artefacts. Four files each carry part of one: . | view | carries | . | package.tgz → package/.index.json | filename, resourceType, id for every file | . | canonicals.json | id, type, url, version, name — canonical resources only | . | artifacts.html | the only source of an artefact’s category | . | package.manifest.json | package-level metadata | . The index is reconstructed, and each field records its source file, because coverage varies: canonicals.json covers about a tenth of one published IG’s artefacts and all of another’s. Two files look like indexes and are not: . | ValueSets.schema.json at the published root is a schema, not an index. It describes an enumeration endpoint’s response and carries an example that holds the list. | openapi/openapi.json is not the IG’s API sidecar set. In at least one published IG it is an unrelated domain API, so an ingest that globs for OpenAPI-shaped files mis-files it. | .

b441059aec3a.title: Where the rules live
b441059aec3a.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . This page describes the content. The rules are skills, and where the two disagree the skill wins and this page is wrong: . | l3-fhir-authoring: authoring FHIR content, and deriving it rather than retyping it. | terminology-management: why terminology has its own lane, and the rule against inventing a code. | fhir-validation: the SUSHI compiler and the validator, and why a missing one is not a pass. | ig-render-jekyll: rendering IG content as folio pages. | . For the tool that compiles and validates all of this, see The FHIR IG Publisher.

c07dedd9aa66.title: The FHIR IG Publisher
c07dedd9aa66.content: TR… . On this page . | How the harness runs it | What one run emits | What only it can do | What it cannot tell you | The version is not pinned | Where the rules live | . This page is generated from docs/source/fhir-ig-publisher/ — each section below links to its own source. ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The FHIR IG Publisher is HL7’s tool that turns an implementation guide’s sources into a published site. Here it is a mechanical actor: a process step with declared inputs and outputs. In a build with pre- and post-processing it is one step among many. API sidecars, JSON Schemas and JSON-LD vocabularies on a published IG are written by scripts after it exits, not by the Publisher.

2b8e6afdbf78.title: How the harness runs it
2b8e6afdbf78.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The harness runs the Publisher once per AST, not once per site build: . | ig-ast-build.sh (the checkout script prepare:fhir-harness) and the reusable ig-ast-refresh.yml run AstExportCli, an entry point added to a fork of the Publisher (litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher). The fork is pinned by its ast-export commit. The run writes output-ast/, one JSON dump per resource. | The site is then rendered from the AST, never from the Publisher’s output/ HTML. No Publisher runs while a site is published. | An IG with no index.config.json, or a run with --bare-ig, takes the bare route instead: the IG’s own ghbuild.yml steps run, and the Publisher’s output is published as it is. | . How to run each route: Render an IG from the command line. How the result is deployed: Publishing an IG.

bca9308ccebe.title: What one run emits
bca9308ccebe.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | output | notes | . | output/ | the rendered site: HTML per resource and per page (input/pagecontent/, sushi-config.yaml pages:) | . | {ResourceType}-{id}.json | the structured surface everything downstream reads | . | .xml, .ttl | the same resource in two more serialisations; this platform reads only the JSON | . | package.tgz → package/.index.json | filename, resourceType, id (index version 2) | . | canonicals.json, package.manifest.json | partial views of the artefact set | . | artifacts.html | the only source of an artefact’s category | . | qa.json | the validation record | . | POT files | translatable strings | . The list changes between releases and the version is not pinned (below), so any count needs a date and a version. It emits no artefact index. ValueSets.schema.json is a schema whose example happens to hold a list; it is not an index. An index must be reconstructed from the four partial views above, and provenance records all four because which one matters differs per IG.

8730585070fe.title: What only it can do
8730585070fe.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | Profile validation: every resource against its profiles and FHIR version. | Dependency-closure resolution with version pinning (for a clinical guideline IG: hl7.terminology, hl7.fhir.uv.extensions.r4, hl7.fhir.uv.cql, hl7.fhir.uv.cpg, hl7.fhir.uv.crmi, hl7.fhir.uv.sdc). | Terminology expansion against a terminology server. | . None can be recomputed from its output, so a cached build is a cache: its indices, dependency edges and versions were true when it was written. Expansion fails quietly. Against a dead or restricted terminology server there are fewer expansions and the consuming steps warn and continue. A thin vocabulary is not evidence of a thin ValueSet; check that expansion ran.

297721951f6b.title: What it cannot tell you
297721951f6b.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Its metadata exports, measured on two IGs: . | export | trust IG | immunizations IG | . | valueset-ref-list.json ValueSet→CodeSystem edges | 17 over 14 | 431 over 252 | . | codesystem-ref-list.json uses populated | 0 of 15 | 0 of 14 | . | usage-stats.json extension→path | 6 | 35 (+5 profiles) | . | uses is declared but never populated, so “no dependencies” and “not computed” look the same. | No dependencies among Library, PlanDefinition or Measure. In the immunizations IG that is 279 + 138 + 41 artefacts, about 61 %: the CQL and decision logic. | . The exports reach terminology, not logic. Logic dependencies need an AST emitted by the tool itself, which means changing org.hl7.fhir.core, not only the Publisher. Re-measure before quoting: a release can close either gap.

135b2d73fac7.title: The version is not pinned
135b2d73fac7.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . A common build fetches the latest publisher.jar on every run: . - name: Update the image to the latest publisher uses: docker://hl7fhir/ig-publisher-base:latest with: args: curl -L https://github.com/HL7/fhir-ig-publisher/releases/latest/download/publisher.jar … . Two builds of the same commit can differ, and the output does not say which version made it, so “the build changed” cannot be told from “the content changed”. A cached AST must therefore record its toolchain (Publisher, core and SUSHI versions) as a required field.

2eb71e38a983.title: fhir-harness
2eb71e38a983.content: The bare FHIR IG pipeline. SUSHI compiles FHIR Shorthand, the IG Publisher builds and validates the guide, and the result is assembled and published to a pages branch. There is no pre-processing and no post-processing, so any FHIR implementation guide can use this layer. input/fsh/ → SUSHI → fsh-generated/resources/ input/pagecontent/ ┐ sushi-config.yaml ┘ → IG Publisher (JVM, Docker) → output/ → pages branch .

2a258e5bc039.title: Publishing an IG
2a258e5bc039.content: TR… . On this page . | The publishing pipeline | Where each output lands | What is published now | Deployment targets: GitHub Pages and Cloudflare | . This page is generated from docs/source/fhir-publishing/ — each section below links to its own source. ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Publishing is the command-line render, run on a GitHub runner and pushed to the IG repository’s gh-pages branch. There is no separate recipe: the workflow runs the same stage-local.ts command that you run by hand. GitHub workflows here are started by hand (workflow_dispatch). Nothing publishes on push.

fcd34a16db35.title: The publishing pipeline
fcd34a16db35.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . input/, sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini │ ig-ast-refresh.yml (reusable; the only writer of the AST cache) ▼ cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id> the AST cache branch │ site-publish.yml → stage-local.ts (no Publisher runs here) ▼ gh-pages: / from the default branch /branches/<branch>/ from any other branch (a preview) │ GitHub Pages ▼ https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/ . | Workflow | Where it lives | What it does | . | ig-ast-refresh.yml | this layer (reusable, workflow_call) | restores the cache and judges it (valid, stale, cannot-tell or missing). If it is not valid, it builds the AST: incrementally when it can, in full otherwise. It seeds the cache branch only from a default-branch commit; otherwise it uploads the AST as an output-ast run artifact | . | templates/ig-repo-site/ig-ast-refresh.yml | copied into the IG repository | the caller. A layer above adds its own pre-export: step and template-repos: here | . | templates/ig-repo-site/site-publish.yml | copied into the IG repository, unchanged | job ast calls the refresh. Job publish mounts the layers from index.lock.json and runs stage-local.ts --repo .; the plan input adds --plan | . | publish-qa.yml | this layer | publishes this layer’s QA results to cat/cat-harness/qa-reports | . The rules (when an AST is valid, who may seed the cache, what a stale AST refuses) are in the ig-build-pipeline skill, §”The AST cache lifecycle”.

ca22587286e1.title: Where each output lands
ca22587286e1.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | Output | Where | Notes | . | the site | gh-pages root | the default-branch publish replaces the root and keeps branches/ and _render-log/ (and anything else the IG lists in site.build.keep) | . | a preview | gh-pages:branches/<branch>/ | carries no binaries | . | the AST | branch cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id> | one orphan commit: the AST, expansions.json and txcache/ | . | the artefact index | <site>/fhir-artifact-index/ | index.json, menu.json, ig-identity.json, releases.json, and package.tgz | . | per-artefact data | <site>/artifact/<Type>-<id>.{html,jsonld,json}, <site>/ast-data/, <site>/<Type>-<id>.json | the thin pages load these | . | build stamp | <site>/folio-build.json | which commit and toolchain built the site | . | release binaries | GitHub release assets | package.tgz, full-ig.zip and the like are never put on gh-pages; releases.json records each asset’s URL and SHA-256 | . Why binaries stay off gh-pages: GitHub Pages serves at most 1 GB. On one measured IG, 966.5 MB of its gh-pages was Publisher binaries copied into branch previews. See the ig-binary-artefacts skill.

2619c955f6ba.title: What is published now
2619c955f6ba.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . This layer itself publishes: . | These pages, on the platform’s documentation site: https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/fhir-harness/. | Its JSON-LD context, which every node it writes points at: https://litlfred.github.io/fhir-harness/ns/context/v1.jsonld. | The reusable workflow and the templates, from the repository: .github/workflows/ and templates/ig-repo-site/. | . An IG built on this layer publishes at its own repository’s Pages address, https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/. Every such site has the same shape: . | Path | What it is | . | / | the IG’s home page | . | /artifacts.html, /toc.html | the artefact list and the table of contents | . | /fhir-artifact-index/index.json | the artefact index, machine-readable | . | /artifact/<Type>-<id>.jsonld | one JSON-LD node per artefact | . | /folio-build.json | the build stamp | . | /branches/<branch>/ | branch previews | . 02da8c31376c.title: Deployment targets: GitHub Pages and Cloudflare
02da8c31376c.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . GitHub Pages is the only target that is built and running. The publisher writes the site to gh-pages, and GitHub serves it. The harness declares the targets it allows, so a new one is a declared option rather than a hidden switch: . | PUBLICATION_HOSTS (in cat-harness-tools schemas/kg/cat-harness.ts): github-pages, local-server, jurisdiction-endpoint or none. A missing value does not default to github-pages. | ARTIFACT_STORE_KINDS (in schemas/sdlc/artifact-store.ts): github-release, object-store (R2, S3 and similar) or site-tree, each with publicBaseUrl, immutableUrls and cacheTtlSeconds. A store that is not declared is refused; it never falls back to GitHub. | The render-kg-to-cdn skill treats each CDN as its own Tool with its own process. Only the GitHub Pages Tool exists today. | . | Option | Status for IG sites | How it would work | . | GitHub Pages | in use | gh-pages branch → https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/. Limits: 1 GB per site, 100 MB per file | . | GitHub Pages + custom domain | available, not set up | a CNAME file on gh-pages and a DNS record. Nothing in the pipeline changes | . | Cloudflare Pages | not set up | connect Cloudflare Pages to the IG repository’s gh-pages branch with no build command, so it serves the same files from Cloudflare’s edge. Nothing in the pipeline changes | . | Cloudflare R2 + CDN | not set up for IG sites | upload the built site, or only the release binaries, to an R2 bucket as an object-store artifact store. This would be a new deploy Tool, run with wrangler | . One layer in this checkout already deploys to Cloudflare: the WHO IRIS mirror’s iris-cdn.yml puts content-addressed files into R2 and keeps its release history in a git repository on Cloudflare. It is a model for an R2 target, not an IG deploy. Two things carry over to any host. The site is built for one base URL (SITE_BASEURL, for example /<repo>), so serving it from another path, such as the root of a custom domain, means building it with that base URL, not copying the files. And Cloudflare Pages caps each deployment’s file count (at the time of writing, 20,000 files on the free plan) and file size (25 MiB). An IG with many artefacts and languages can pass the cap, so count the files on gh-pages first. Before choosing Cloudflare, decide three things: who holds the API token (it is a repository secret, never in a file); whether previews (branches/) move too or stay on GitHub; and whether the canonical URL changes. A canonical URL that moves breaks every link already published.

7e3de1dcb22b.title: Render an IG from the command line
7e3de1dcb22b.content: TR… . On this page . | Harnessed or bare: two routes | What you need installed | The one command | Step by step | Settings the steps read | When it refuses | . This page is generated from docs/source/fhir-run-locally/ — each section below links to its own source. ✎ Edit QA… TR… . This page says how to render an implementation guide through the harness from a terminal, on your own machine or in an agent’s container. The output is the same just-the-docs site the publish workflow deploys. A harnessed render has two halves: . | Build the IG’s AST once. This is the only step that runs the IG Publisher. It writes output-ast/, one JSON dump per resource. | Render the site from that AST. The harness never reads the Publisher’s output/ HTML. The AST is the one input to the site build. | . The steps below are listed in that order. To deploy the result, see Publishing an IG.

7a60fc11a366.doc: Render an IG from the command line
7a60fc11a366.title: Harnessed or bare: two routes
7a60fc11a366.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . |   | Harnessed (this layer) | Bare (the IG Publisher alone) | . | When it is taken | the IG repository has an index.config.json naming its landing layer, "site": { "landing": "<layer>" } | the repository has no index.config.json, or you pass --bare-ig | . | What runs the Publisher | AstExportCli, an entry point added to a fork of the Publisher (litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher), pinned by commit | the repository’s own ghbuild.yml steps (stock publisher.jar, latest release) | . | What the site is built from | the AST (output-ast/, or the cache branch) | the Publisher’s output/ as it lays it out | . | What you get | thin just-the-docs pages, a JSON-LD node per artefact, the artefact index, search, a language picker | the Publisher’s HTML | . | Version pinned? | yes: SUSHI, Java and Node in scripts/ig-toolchain.env; the Publisher by the ast-export commit | no: the version floats (see the IG Publisher) | . Both routes start with one command, stage-local.ts. It takes the harnessed route whenever it can. Do not pass --bare-ig to a harnessed IG unless you want the Publisher’s own pages.

02a0d7619ca3.doc: Render an IG from the command line
02a0d7619ca3.title: What you need installed
02a0d7619ca3.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | Tool | Needed for | Notes | . | bun | every step | the harness’s runtime; use the version in cat-harness/.bun-version | . | git, bash, curl | every step |   | . | Java 17, mvn | building the AST | Maven compiles AstExportCli from the Publisher fork | . | Node 20, npm | building the AST | for SUSHI 3.21.0, which the build script installs if missing | . | Ruby, gem | building the AST and rendering | Jekyll, which the build script installs if missing | . | python3 with venv | rendering | checked by stage-local.ts before it starts | . | Docker | bare route only | when the IG’s own workflow runs the Publisher in a container image | . Building the AST also needs network access to packages.fhir.org, the terminology server (default http://tx.fhir.org) and Maven Central. If packages.fhir.org is refused, see the fhir-validation skill, §”When a package host refuses you”. The layers come from the IG’s index.lock.json, and you do not mount them by hand. The IG’s cat script is bun .github/cat.ts: on a fresh clone, the first bun run cat … mounts every layer the lock pins, then runs the command. It fetches the mounter at the commit the lock pins and checks each layer’s hash before keeping it. Later runs find the layers on disk and go straight to the command. After a re-pin, or to mount without running anything, run bash .github/mount-from-lock.sh from the IG’s root. It replaces a stale mount and reports an intact one as current. An IG set up before this has "cat": "bun cat-harness-tools/scripts/run-script.ts" and no .github/cat.ts. Copy cat.ts and mount-from-lock.sh from cat-harness-tools/templates/root-bootstrap/ into its .github/ and set "cat": "bun .github/cat.ts".

2953a05f376f.doc: Render an IG from the command line
2953a05f376f.title: The one command
2953a05f376f.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . From the IG repository’s root. On a fresh clone the first command mounts the layers before it runs (what you need installed says how): . # 1. Build the AST (one Publisher run; minutes to tens of minutes) bun run cat prepare:fhir-harness # 2. See what would be built and where, and stop bun run cat stage:local --repo . --plan # 3. Build the site and compose the publish commit, pushing nothing bun run cat stage:local --repo . --dry-run . bun run cat <name> runs a script that any mounted layer declares. The IG’s cat script is bun .github/cat.ts, which mounts the layers when they are missing and then hands over to cat-harness-tools/scripts/run-script.ts. prepare:fhir-harness is bash fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast-build.sh --ig-root ., and stage:local is cat-harness-tools/scripts/stage-local.ts. Other ways to finish: . | Command | What it does | . | bun run cat stage:local --repo . --artifact <dir> | writes a bundle you can open as a page, instead of pushing | . | bun run cat stage:local --repo . | publishes. On the default branch it publishes the site root; on any other branch, a preview at branches/<branch>/ | . You can skip step 1 when the IG’s cache branch already holds an AST that is valid for your commit: the render restores it.

5e3aacae05d7.doc: Render an IG from the command line
5e3aacae05d7.title: Step by step
5e3aacae05d7.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . stage-local.ts runs these named steps in order. The layers supply them, so you can also run any one of them on its own with bun run cat <step>: . | # | Step | Script | What it does | . | 1 | ig-site:ast | ig-repo-site.ts ast | restores the AST from the cache branch cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id> (or keeps a valid output-ast/), and refuses a stale one | . | 2 | ig-site:sidecars | the landing layer’s own | optional: API sidecars from the AST, when the landing layer has this step | . | 3 | ig-index:build | build-ig-indexes.ts | the artefact index, menu and releases in fhir-artifact-index/ | . | 4 | ig-site:compose | ig-repo-site.ts compose | the thin artefact pages, with the IG’s own pages composed at the site root | . | 5 | ig-site:openapi | cat-harness-tools | optional: a page per OpenAPI operation, when the IG has openapi/cat-openapi.config.json | . | 6 | ig-site:publisher-pages | ig-repo-site.ts publisher-pages | serves the AST’s data, guards against leftover Publisher chrome, stamps the build | . | 7 | ig-site:bar | ig-repo-site.ts bar | the language picker and the IG’s slim bar | . The scripts’ own usage lines: . ig-repo-site.ts ast [--ig <checkout>] [--work <dir>] ig-repo-site.ts compose <site source> [--ig <checkout>] [--baseurl <base>] [--plantuml-jar <jar>] [--work <dir>] ig-repo-site.ts publisher-pages <built site> [--ig <checkout>] [--work <dir>] ig-repo-site.ts bar <built site> [--ig <checkout>] ig-ast-build.sh [--ig-root DIR] [--tx URL] [--ast-export-ref SHA] [--work DIR] [--template-repo ID=OWNER/REPO]… . To publish an AST you built yourself to the cache branch, so the next render and CI can reuse it (only from a default-branch commit): . bash fhir-harness/scripts/ig-cache.sh seed --ig-root . --push .

bf70efecb402.doc: Render an IG from the command line
bf70efecb402.title: Settings the steps read
bf70efecb402.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | Variable | Read by | Meaning | . | SITE_WORK | ig-repo-site.ts | working directory; the default for --work | . | FOLIO_SITE_BASEURL | ig-repo-site.ts compose | the site’s base URL when --baseurl is not given | . | SITE_ACCEPT_STALE_AST=1 | ig-repo-site.ts ast | accept a stale AST. Use it for a preview only; never for the site root | . | IG_TEMPLATE_REPOS | ig-ast-build.sh | extra --template-repo ID=OWNER/REPO values, for an IG template that is not on the CI build server | . | TMPDIR | ig-ast-build.sh | where the work directory goes (default $TMPDIR/ig-ast-build) | . stage-local.ts sets the others itself (SITE_INSTANCE, SITE_BASEURL, SITE_URL, SITE_SOURCE, SITE_DIR and the rest) when it calls each step.

d243d5252f63.doc: Render an IG from the command line
d243d5252f63.title: When it refuses
d243d5252f63.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | Message or symptom | Cause | What to do | . | cat: mounting failed | the mounter could not fetch a layer, or a layer’s bytes did not match the lock | run bash .github/mount-from-lock.sh to see which layer and why | . | the AST is stale, cannot-tell, or missing | no AST matches your commit’s inputs | run bun run cat prepare:fhir-harness, or the ig-ast-refresh workflow | . | index.config.json has no site.landing | the IG is harnessed but does not say which layer’s chrome it wears | add "site": { "landing": "<layer>" } | . | a prerequisite is missing | docker, python3 -m venv, bash or curl was not found | install it; the plan names which one | . | ig-ast-build: the AST just built is not valid | the inputs changed during the build | commit or stash, then build again | . | the Publisher cannot fetch a package | packages.fhir.org is unreachable | see the fhir-validation skill, §”When a package host refuses you” | . Exit codes of ig-ast-site.sh: 1 means no AST could be restored; 3 means the AST was restored but could not be turned into pages.
